sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Flow cytometry with anti-FLAG mAb confirmed robust cell-surface display; no functional assay reported in the clips.
sites.rationale: CLEC2L is a type II transmembrane protein (intracellular 1–68, TM 69–89, extracellular 90–214); the C-terminus at position 214 is therefore extracellular, 125 residues from the TM boundary. The paper names the tag position only as 'C-terminal'/'carboxyterminal', so the junction is topology-derived: there is exactly one C-terminus, at residue 214 (T). Python confirmed seq[213]='T'. Anti-FLAG flow cytometry on intact cells demonstrates the tag is accessible on the extracellular face. Full-length human CLEC2L with a C-terminal FLAG tag expressed in 293T cells; anti-FLAG flow cytometry confirmed surface display of the tagged construct. L2 corroborates with the mouse ortholog C-terminally FLAG-tagged and detected identically. Both clips are from the same paper (PMC3679072).

sources.claim: Flow cytometric analyses of transiently transfected 293T cells revealed that the CLEC2L -encoded FLAG-tagged CTLR is readily expressed at the cell surface ( Figure 3A ).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are two clips from the same paper (PMC3679072) describing the same experimental approach on human (L1) and mouse (L2) CLEC2L; L1 is used as the primary supporting clip. Neither clip names a specific residue number, so position_evidence is topology_derived rather than validated. No clips in the ledger address the intracellular N-terminus, any internal loop, or any function-abrogating insertion, so other_positions is empty.
